newsitem.title: BRAZIL: INTERVIEW-Banco de Boston to grow in retail market.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Banco de Boston to grow in retail market.

text.p: Bank of Boston Corp's Brazil unit Banco de Boston aims to expand its retail business and strengthen its investment banking activities, said the bank's new president, Carlos Craide.

"The idea is to expand the bank's retail business and strengthen its position as investment bank, particularly in the international capital markets," said Craide, hired to run Banco de Boston's day-to-day operations.

Craide, an executive director of Citicorp's Citibank Brazil subsidiary, will replace Henrique Meirelles, who will take over as Bank of Boston's president and chief operating officer early next month in the U.S.
Banco de Boston plans to increase its number of individual and corporate clients, attracting small and medium-sized firms by offering financing, he said.
Craide sees growing demand for credit as the economy keeps stabilizing under the country's two-year old anti-inflation Real Plan.

"There is a great potential for consumer indebtedness in Brazil," he said, noting that Brazilians on average owe only the equivalent of one month's salary, while in other countries with stable economies individuals owe over one year's salary.

Currently, Banco de Boston has 42,000 of what the bank calls full-bank clients and around 200,000 clients for specific products. Its target is to reach 100,000 full bank clients and one million product clients by 2000.
Regarding capital markets, Craide said the bank plans to focus on securitizations, bonds and equity issues.
Craide, 49, was responsible for Corporate Banking and Products at Citibank Brazil, where he worked for 22 years.
Between 1994 and 1995, Craide worked in Citibank's headquarters in New York.
